history.title: Transaction History
history.help_what: The history is the complete record of all transactions you have participated in, either as sender (who sends) or as recipient (who receives). It includes transfers between users, payments and any other movement of Trueques ({{currency}}) from your account.
history.help_purpose: To keep track of your movements, verify who has sent you or who you have sent Trueques to, review the reasons for each transaction and audit that everything matches your expectations. It is your personal account book within the network.
history.help_usage: When you enter the page, the list of your most recent transactions is loaded automatically. Each row is a transaction. If nothing appears, it means you have not yet made or received any transfers.
history.help_col_date: Day the transaction was made (YYYY-MM-DD format). E.g: 2024-06-15.
history.help_col_from: Identifier of the user who sent the Trueques. If it's you, it means you sent money. E.g: @juan@localhost.
history.help_col_to: Identifier of the user who received the Trueques. If it's you, it means you received money. E.g: @maria@localhost.
history.help_col_amount: Amount of Trueques ({{currency}}) transferred in that operation. 1 {{currency}} = 1 kWh of energy. E.g: 50 {{currency}}.
history.help_col_ref: Reference or note that the sender left to explain the reason for the payment. May be empty if no note was left. E.g: "Payment for bakery".
history.help_filter: Currently the history shows all your transactions ordered by date. If you need to find a specific one, use the browser search function (Ctrl+F) to find by username, amount or reference.
history.help_hash: Each transaction has a cryptographic identifier (hash) that makes it unique and unalterable. This means that once registered, no one can modify its data (amount, sender, recipient) without being detected. The hash guarantees that the history is reliable and that transactions have not been tampered with.
history.help_note: The system sums to zero. If someone sent 50 {{currency}}, their balance went down 50 and the recipient's went up 50 (minus tax if applicable). The total of all balances in the network is always zero: no money is created or destroyed.
history.empty_hint: Transactions appear when you transfer or receive Trueques. Go to Transfer or Payments to make a transaction.

calculator.title: Price Calculator
calculator.help_what: It is a tool that calculates the fair price of a product or service based on its real energy cost. The price in {{currency}} equals the total energy invested in producing it: 1 {{currency}} = 1 kWh. There is no profit or speculation: the price reflects the work and materials.
calculator.help_purpose: It serves to determine the energy price of any product or service before proposing it to the assembly. This way all prices are fair, transparent and comparable. You take the result to the assembly for approval and addition to the catalog.
calculator.help_usage: You have two modes. The Easy mode guides you with a questionnaire: you select the type of work, the hours, and the materials you used; the system calculates everything. The Advanced mode allows you to enter the energy values directly in kWh if you know them.
calculator.help_direct: It is the energy consumed directly in the process: electricity, gas or fuel used in production. Example: 2 kWh of electricity to bake bread.
calculator.help_human: It is the energy of the human work invested. It is calculated by multiplying the hours worked by the energy rate (vital basket / hours per day). Example: 3 hours of work x 1.0 TQ/hour (base rate) = 3.0 TQ. Effort factors adjust upward for harder work.
calculator.help_inputs: It is the energy incorporated in the materials and raw materials used. Each input has an energy cost per unit. Example: 1 kg of flour = 1.8 kWh, 0.5 kg of salt = 0.35 kWh.
calculator.help_effort: It is a multiplier that adjusts the cost if the work is especially difficult or easy. 1.0 = normal, 1.5 = 50% more effort, 0.8 = 20% less. Example: Digging earth at 40°C has factor 1.5.
calculator.help_final: Price = (Direct energy + Human energy + Input energy + Amortization) x Effort factor x Rate. The result is the suggested price in {{currency}}.
calculator.step1_title: Step 1: What work did you do?
calculator.step1_desc: Select the type of work and how many hours you worked. The system knows how much energy each type of work uses.
calculator.work_category_hint: Categories and types are managed in Calculator Parameters.

recovery_page.title: Account Recovery
recovery_page.help_what_desc: Account recovery is the process by which a user who lost access to their account (forgot password, lost device with passkey, etc.) can regain access to the system safely.
recovery_page.help_how_desc: No one can restore access on their own. A recovery request is created and several people must approve it before it completes. This prevents someone malicious from impersonating another user. The more approvals required, the more secure (but slower) the process.
recovery_page.help_codes_desc: Invitation codes are unique keys that allow a new user to join the node. In the context of recovery, they serve as a verification mechanism: only someone with a valid code can prove they were legitimately invited and therefore has the right to recover their account.
recovery_page.help_multisig_desc: It is the approval mode where N distinct members must sign (approve) the request. For example, if 3 approvals are configured, at least 3 different members must press "Approve" before the account is restored. No single person has the power to restore accounts.
recovery_page.help_mode_multisig: Multi-signature: N signatures from any member (configurable, minimum 2)
recovery_page.help_mode_council: Council: Approval by a designated group of trusted people
recovery_page.help_mode_assembly: Assembly: Vote in assembly by majority
recovery_page.help_usage_desc: Press "New Request" to create a recovery indicating the user and the reason. Pending requests appear in the list: you can approve, reject or view signature details. From "Configuration" you can adjust the approval mode and parameters.
recovery_page.config_form_desc: No single person can restore access. Minimum 2 approvals required.

calculator_params.help_approval_desc: Todo parametro nuevo o modificado queda en estado "Pendiente" y debe ser aprobado por asamblea. Los parametros no aprobados no aparecen en la calculadora. Un usuario con permiso de gestion (calculator.manage_params) puede aprobarlos con el boton de check verde. Esto asegura que la comunidad valide cada cambio en el sistema de precios.
calculator_params.help_categories_desc: Agrupan parametros similares para encontrarlos facil. Por ejemplo: "Construccion" agrupa albañileria, plomeria, electricidad; "Alimentos" agrupa harina, azucar, verduras. Puedes crear nuevas categorias segun las necesidades de tu nodo.
calculator_params.help_currency_desc: Los costos se expresan en kWh (1
calculator_params.help_currency_desc2: El simbolo de tu moneda local es "
calculator_params.help_currency_desc3: " y aparece en los textos de ayuda de los campos.
calculator_params.help_effort_desc: Multiplicador adicional sobre el esfuerzo base de la categoria. 1.0 = sin cambio. Usalo para trabajos mas dificiles (1.3 = 30% mas) o mas faciles (0.8 = 20% menos) de lo normal para su categoria. Por ejemplo: cavar tierra a 40°C podria tener factor 1.3 sobre la categoria agricola.
calculator_params.help_materials_desc: Definen cuanto energia cuesta cada material que se usa en la produccion. Por ejemplo: harina de trigo = 1.8 kWh/kg, madera = 2.5 kWh/m3, electricidad = 1.0 kWh/kWh. Estos valores representan la energia total invertida en producir, transportar y almacenar cada insumo.
calculator_params.help_purpose_desc: Aqui se gestionan todos los tipos de trabajo e insumos que usa la calculadora de precios. Puedes crear, editar, aprobar y desactivar parametros, asi como organizarlos en categorias. Es el panel de control del sistema de precios del nodo.
calculator_params.help_usage_desc: 1) Selecciona la pestana "Tipos de Trabajo" o "Insumos/Materiales" segun lo que quieras gestionar. 2) Usa el buscador y el filtro de categoria para encontrar parametros existentes. 3) Crea categorias nuevas si las necesitas. 4) Crea parametros nuevos con el boton "Nuevo Parametro". 5) Aprueba los parametros pendientes con el boton de check verde. 6) Edita o elimina parametros existentes segun sea necesario.
calculator_params.help_what_desc: Los parametros son los valores de referencia que usa la calculadora de precios para determinar el costo energetico (en kWh) de cualquier trabajo o insumo. Sin estos parametros, la calculadora no puede asignar un precio justo a los productos y servicios del nodo. Cada parametro define cuanto energia representa una unidad de trabajo o de material.
calculator_params.help_who_desc: Solo los usuarios con el permiso "calculator.manage_params" pueden crear, editar, aprobar y eliminar parametros. El resto de usuarios puede verlos pero no modificarlos. La aprobacion final requiere decision asamblearia.
calculator_params.help_work_types: Tipos de trabajo (dinamicos segun tarifa energetica):
calculator_params.help_work_types_desc: Cada tipo de trabajo se vincula a una categoria de esfuerzo (agricola, tecnico, administrativo). El costo en kWh se calcula automaticamente desde la canasta vital:
calculator_params.help_work_types_desc2: , y cada categoria tiene su factor de esfuerzo (agricola=0.61, tecnico=3.0, admin=1.0). Si la asamblea cambia la canasta vital, todos los trabajos se actualizan automaticamente. Tambien puedes especificar un factor de amplificacion adicional para trabajos mas dificiles o faciles de lo normal.

fund.help_what: El Fondo Comunitario ES la cuenta de la Asamblea General. No son cuentas separadas: es una sola cuenta que recibe los impuestos y sirve como tesoro comunitario.
fund.help_transfer: Puedes transferir a esta cuenta usando cualquiera de estos 3 nombres (todos llegan a la misma cuenta): @asamblea, @impuestos o @fondo_comunitario.
fund.help_source: Cada vez que alguien hace una transferencia, el sistema aplica un porcentaje de impuesto automatico que va a parar a esta cuenta. Por ejemplo, si el impuesto es 2% y se transfieren 100 unidades, 2 unidades van al fondo. Nadie necesita depositar manualmente: se acumula solo con el uso.
fund.help_usage: El dinero del fondo se destina a infraestructura del nodo, servicios publicos, ayuda mutua entre miembros, y proyectos aprobados por la asamblea. No puede gastarse libremente: cada gasto requiere aprobacion colectiva.
fund.help_distribute: Para gastar dinero del fondo hay que crear una propuesta de distribucion indicando el destinatario, el monto y la razon. Luego los miembros votan a favor o en contra. Si la propuesta se aprueba, se puede ejecutar y el dinero se transfiere al destinatario.
fund.help_admin: Nadie individualmente. El balance es visible para todos, pero los gastos solo se realizan mediante votacion de la asamblea. Esto garantiza que el fondo no pueda ser mal utilizado por una sola persona.
